title: Impact of Medicaid Expansion on Uninsured Rates

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy

**Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)**

This is a classic DID setup: we have treated states (Medicaid expansion) vs. control states (no expansion), observed before and after policy implementation. The dataset explicitly provides the `treated`, `post`, and `treat_x_post` interaction term.

**Key Assumption: Parallel Trends** — In the absence of Medicaid expansion, the uninsured rate trends in expansion states would have evolved similarly to those in non-expansion states. We can partially assess this by examining pre-treatment period trends across groups.

**Estimating Equation:**
$$y_{it} = \alpha + \beta_1 \cdot \text{treated}_i + \beta_2 \cdot \text{post}_t + \delta \cdot (\text{treated}_i \times \text{post}_t) + \epsilon_{it}$$

where $\delta$ is the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT) — the causal effect of Medicaid expansion on the log uninsured rate.

## 2. R Code

```r
# =============================================================
# DID Analysis: Impact of Medicaid Expansion on Uninsured Rates
# =============================================================

library(fixest)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)
library(ggplot2)

# --- Load Data ---
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s31_data.csv")
cat("=== Data Overview ===\n")
str(df)
cat("\nDimensions:", nrow(df), "x", ncol(df), "\n")
summary(df)

# Check panel structure
cat("\n=== Panel Structure ===\n")
cat("Unique units:", length(unique(df$unit_id)), "\n")
cat("Unique periods:", sort(unique(df$period)), "\n")
cat("Treated units:", sum(df$treated[!duplicated(df$unit_id)]), "\n")
cat("Control units:", sum(1 - df$treated[!duplicated(df$unit_id)]), "\n")

# Group means
cat("\n=== Group Means of y (log uninsured rate) ===\n")
group_means <- aggregate(y ~ treated + post, data = df, FUN = mean)
print(group_means)

# Manual DID calculation
y00 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 0])
y01 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 0 & df$post == 1])
y10 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 0])
y11 <- mean(df$y[df$treated == 1 & df$post == 1])
did_manual <- (y11 - y10) - (y01 - y00)
cat("\n=== Manual DID Calculation ===\n")
cat("Control: pre =", round(y00, 4), ", post =", round(y01, 4), ", diff =", round(y01 - y00, 4), "\n")
cat("Treated: pre =", round(y10, 4), ", post =", round(y11, 4), ", diff =", round(y11 - y10, 4), "\n")
cat("DID estimate (manual):", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")

# =============================================================
# Model 1: Basic OLS DID
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== Model 1: Basic OLS DID ===\n")
model1 <- lm(y ~ treated + post + treat_x_post, data = df)
summary(model1)

# =============================================================
# Model 2: DID with robust (HC1) standard errors
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== Model 2: DID with Robust SEs ===\n")
robust_se <- coeftest(model1, vcov = vcovHC(model1, type = "HC1"))
print(robust_se)

# =============================================================
# Model 3: DID with unit and period fixed effects (using fixest)
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== Model 3: Two-Way Fixed Effects DID ===\n")
model3 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, data = df)
summary(model3)

# =============================================================
# Model 4: Cluster standard errors at unit level
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== Model 4: TWFE with Clustered SEs at Unit Level ===\n")
model4 <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period, 
                data = df, cluster = ~unit_id)
summary(model4)

# =============================================================
# Robustness Check 1: Parallel Trends (pre-treatment only)
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Pre-Treatment Means ===\n")
pre_data <- df[df$post == 0, ]
cat("Pre-treatment mean (treated):", round(mean(pre_data$y[pre_data$treated == 1]), 4), "\n")
cat("Pre-treatment mean (control):", round(mean(pre_data$y[pre_data$treated == 0]), 4), "\n")
# With only 2 periods we can't do a full event study, but we check balance
t_test_pre <- t.test(y ~ treated, data = pre_data)
cat("t-test p-value for pre-treatment difference:", round(t_test_pre$p.value, 4), "\n")

# =============================================================
# Robustness Check 2: Permutation / Placebo test
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== Robustness: Placebo Test (random treatment assignment) ===\n")
set.seed(42)
n_perms <- 1000
placebo_coefs <- numeric(n_perms)
unit_ids <- unique(df$unit_id)
n_treated <- sum(df$treated[!duplicated(df$unit_id)])

for (i in 1:n_perms) {
  fake_treated_units <- sample(unit_ids, n_treated)
  df$fake_treated <- as.integer(df$unit_id %in% fake_treated_units)
  df$fake_interaction <- df$fake_treated * df$post
  pmod <- lm(y ~ fake_treated + post + fake_interaction, data = df)
  placebo_coefs[i] <- coef(pmod)["fake_interaction"]
}
actual_coef <- coef(model1)["treat_x_post"]
p_value_perm <- mean(abs(placebo_coefs) >= abs(actual_coef))
cat("Actual DID coefficient:", round(actual_coef, 4), "\n")
cat("Permutation p-value:", round(p_value_perm, 4), "\n")
cat("Placebo distribution: mean =", round(mean(placebo_coefs), 4),
    ", sd =", round(sd(placebo_coefs), 4), "\n")

# =============================================================
# Summary of All Results
# =============================================================
cat("\n=== ========================================= ===\n")
cat("=== SUMMARY OF DID ESTIMATES ===\n")
cat("=== ========================================= ===\n")
cat("Manual DID:                     ", round(did_manual, 4), "\n")
cat("OLS DID (treat_x_post):         ", round(coef(model1)["treat_x_post"], 4),
    " (p =", round(summary(model1)$coefficients["treat_x_post", 4], 4), ")\n")
cat("Robust SE DID:                  ", round(robust_se["treat_x_post", 1], 4),
    " (p =", round(robust_se["treat_x_post", 4], 4), ")\n")
cat("TWFE DID:                       ", round(coef(model3)["treat_x_post"], 4), "\n")
cat("TWFE DID (clustered SE):        ", round(coef(model4)["treat_x_post"], 4),
    " (p =", round(pvalue(model4)["treat_x_post"], 4), ")\n")
cat("Permutation test p-value:       ", round(p_value_perm, 4), "\n")
cat("\nInterpretation: A coefficient of", round(actual_coef, 4),
    "means Medicaid expansion\nchanged the log uninsured rate by",
    round(actual_coef, 4), "units,\nor approximately a",
    round((exp(actual_coef) - 1) * 100, 2), "% change in the uninsured rate.\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings

**Expected Sign:** **Negative.** Medicaid expansion provides insurance coverage to previously uninsured individuals (particularly those earning up to 138% of the federal poverty level), so we expect the uninsured rate to decrease in expansion states relative to non-expansion states.

**Expected Magnitude:** The DID coefficient ($\delta$) on `treat_x_post` should be negative and statistically significant. Since the outcome is the **log** uninsured rate, a coefficient around **-0.2 to -0.5** would be plausible, corresponding to roughly a 20–40% reduction in the uninsured rate. Empirical literature on ACA Medicaid expansion typically finds substantial reductions (3–7 percentage point decreases in uninsured rates), which aligns with this range in log terms depending on baseline levels.

**Robustness expectations:**
- Results should be consistent across OLS, robust SE, and TWFE specifications (with only 2 periods, TWFE and basic DID should yield identical treatment effect estimates).
- The permutation test should confirm that the actual coefficient falls in the extreme tail of the placebo distribution, reinforcing a causal interpretation.
- Pre-treatment group differences may exist in levels (expansion states may have had different baseline uninsured rates), but the parallel trends assumption requires similar *trends*, not identical levels.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Compare changes in uninsured rates over time between treated and untreated states.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The expansion of Medicaid coverage significantly reduces the uninsured rate.
